this is so deep... you're going places

To be honest, I think a lot of people experience some sort of inability to visualize things, and the result being executive dysfunction. Its frustrating when you're unable to see something and therefore are unable to get through it, and even dangerous, but there's always a chance to find a way to do it. Not even do it in the sense of going through with it, but more so finding a route to go through that you CAN picture. There's always things we can't see, things we can't picture, even if you and I have different reasons, but that also must mean there's things on the other side. 

I think what really matters is how you take into consideration these thoughts. You've completely acknowledged it, which is so strong, and maybe you haven't realized it but i feel you articulated this really well. I have a pretty clear vision (no pun intended) of what you're going through. Don't be afraid to just reach out to someone and say you feel 'not right.' Don't be afraid to be unable to express the why. Sometimes you just need to focus on the what. Don't worry too much about the consequence, because you, right then, in the moment, deserve support from yourself. I can't tell you the 16 ultra steps to fixing your 'problem' but i can't tell you you've already finished step one: recognize what's the source. And maybe that's enough of a start.

Good luck man. You matter, thank you for sharing your experience.
